svg.title: SDLC plugin layers
svg.desc: Layer map of the sdlc plugin by structure, sdlc 2.0. Top to bottom: 16 commands, 10 skills grouped by orchestrator phase (Define, Build, Review, Ship with Learn), with the orchestrator's references/ holding one file per phase and the former worktree, parallel-agent, code-review-reception and branch-finishing skills; 6 agents (code-reviewer and ui-reviewer for Review, pr-test-analyzer and silent-failure-hunter for /review-pr, qa-tester on request, code-explorer for brownfield setup); scripts (verify.py proves a feature, state.py moves it); templates (intent, spec, plan, review, backlog); and the files written into the user's repo (.sdlc/, docs/sdlc/, .claude/, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, knowledge/). Hooks (security-guidance, hookify, verify-freshness, prove-budget, model-router with role-guard and trust-anchor) run on six Claude Code events outside the stack, each started through sg-python.sh. Packaging, the other hosts' manifests, tests, docs and licenses sit underneath. At the bottom, the optional sdlc-extras companion plugin (plugins/sdlc-extras/, installed separately from the same marketplace) holds the Ralph loop with its Stop hook and setup script, hookify's list, configure and help commands, and the conversation-analyzer, type-design-analyzer, comment-analyzer, code-simplifier and feature-reviewer agents.
svg.text: How sdlc 2.0 is built, from what the user types down to what lands in their repo. Each band is one plugin structure and arrows show who calls whom.
Hooks sit outside the stack because Claude Code fires them, not the workflow.
start hands the feature to the orchestrator; other commands load one skill or run a script
